headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed flow execution make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads and writes local files, MCP configs, hooks, and session state, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if ECC outputs are fed into Langflow or vice versa. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are copied into a Langflow flow node as prompt text
IF Langflow uploads a file that ECC later reads as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate the two tools into different workspaces
Disable automatic file ingestion between them
Add a manual review step before any prompt-like content is reused
Use provenance tags on all shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while Langflow stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials on the server filesystem. If they share a workspace or files are moved between them, sensitive material can flow from ECC into Langflow outputs or stores. This is a default-configuration concern, not merely unusual setup.
conditions: IF ECC session files or security findings are imported into Langflow
IF Langflow stores contain credentials or sensitive flow inputs that ECC can read from the same filesystem
mitigations: Keep ECC and Langflow on separate hosts or containers
Restrict shared directories to non-sensitive artifacts
Rotate any credentials copied into Langflow stores
Review file permissions on both runtimes
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning at import/export boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use MCP; Langflow can also write the filesystem and run unsandboxed Python code by default. If both operate on the same repo or server directory, concurrent writes and state changes can corrupt files or overwrite each other's outputs. The overlap is broad and dangerous in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or server filesystem
IF Langflow flows execute Python components while ECC edits the same files or git branch
mitigations: Assign separate directories and git branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent edits during shared runs
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a flow orchestrator, so it can treat upstream outputs as inputs to later nodes. ECC produces code, docs, and security findings, which Langflow may then route into actions or model calls without verification. That makes erroneous ECC output likely to cascade into downstream automated steps.
conditions: IF a Langflow node consumes ECC-generated text without validation
IF the flow uses ECC outputs to trigger API calls or code execution
mitigations: Insert a validation node before any action-taking step
Require human approval for destructive branches
Limit ECC output to structured schemas
Log and diff intermediate outputs
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles security findings, git history, and session artifacts, while Langflow stores flow inputs and credentials server-side. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different retention and storage surfaces that can create compliance gaps if the same regulated data class is routed through both. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ECC session artifacts and then persisted in Langflow stores
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same data class across the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between tools
Avoid storing regulated data in either system
Align retention settings across both systems
Document deletion/export procedures
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for shared data classes
